If all trees on earth were pens and the sea ink, replenished by seven more seas, Allah's words would still not be exhausted.
Creating and resurrecting all people is, for Allah, like doing so for a single soul.
Allah merges night into day, runs the sun and moon, and sails ships to show His signs; amid waves people call on Him sincerely, but once ashore some stay moderate.
People are told to fear their Lord and a Day when no father or son can help the other, and not be deluded by worldly life or the Deceiver.
Allah alone knows the Hour, sends the rain and knows what is in wombs, while no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or where it will die.
The Book is revealed beyond doubt from the Lord of the worlds, not invented but the truth, so the Prophet may warn a people who had no warner before.
Allah created the heavens and earth in six days, established Himself above the Throne, arranges every matter, and made man from clay, proportioning him and giving hearing, sight and hearts.
Disbelievers ask if they will be created anew after being lost in the earth; the angel of death will take them, and then they return to their Lord.
Criminals will hang their heads before their Lord begging to return, but Allah will fill Hell with jinn and people, who taste eternal punishment for forgetting this Day.
Believers in Allah's verses prostrate when reminded, shun arrogance, rise from bed to call on their Lord in fear and hope, spend, and have hidden comfort as reward.
Believers and the defiantly disobedient are not equal: believers have the Gardens of Refuge, the disobedient the Fire, and a nearer punishment short of the greater, that perhaps they repent.
None is more unjust than one reminded of his Lord's verses who turns away, and Allah will take retribution from the criminals.
Allah gave Moses the Scripture and made the Torah guidance for the Children of Israel, raised patient guiding leaders among them, and will judge their differences on Resurrection Day.
Many generations were destroyed before them, whose dwellings they walk among, and in that are signs, if they would hear.
Allah drives water to barren land and brings forth crops that feed their livestock and themselves, if they would see.
Disbelievers ask when the conquest will be; then their belief will not benefit them nor will they be reprieved, so the Prophet is to turn away and wait.
The Prophet is told to fear Allah, not obey the disbelievers and hypocrites, follow what is revealed to him, and rely on Allah.
Wives declared unlawful do not become mothers, nor adopted sons true sons; adopted children are called by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion if unknown.
The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves and his wives are their mothers, while blood relatives are more entitled to inherit than other believers and emigrants.
Allah took a solemn covenant from the prophets, including the Prophet, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, to question the truthful about their truth, and prepared punishment for disbelievers.
Believers are reminded how Allah sent a wind and unseen armies against the Confederates who came from above and below, when eyes shifted, hearts reached throats and believers were shaken.

At the Trench, hypocrites called Allah's promise delusion, urged Yathrib's people home, sought leave claiming exposed houses, held back from battle, and lashed believers with sharp tongues once fear passed.
The Messenger of Allah is an excellent example for anyone hoping in Allah and the Last Day and remembering Allah often.
Seeing the companies, believers said Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth and grew in faith; some have fulfilled their vow and others await, and Allah rewards the truthful.
Allah repelled the disbelieving Confederates in their rage with no gain, and He sufficed the believers in battle.
Allah brought the Confederates' supporters among the People of the Scripture down from their fortresses, some killed and some captured, and gave the believers their land, homes and properties.
The Prophet's wives are to choose worldly adornment or Allah and the Hereafter, face double punishment or reward, speak properly, stay in their houses, pray, give zakah and obey.
Allah has prepared forgiveness and great reward for Muslim and believing men and women who are obedient, truthful, patient, humble, charitable, fasting, chaste and remember Allah often.
When Allah and His Messenger decide a matter, no believing man or woman has a choice in it, and whoever disobeys them has clearly strayed.
Once Zayd no longer needed his wife Zaynab, Allah married her to the Prophet, removing believers' discomfort over adopted sons' wives; Muhammad is Allah's Messenger and last of the prophets.
Believers are told to remember Allah much and exalt Him morning and afternoon; He blesses them to bring them into light, and their greeting on meeting Him will be Peace.
The Prophet is sent as witness, bringer of good tidings, warner, caller to Allah and illuminating lamp, told not to obey disbelievers and hypocrites but to rely on Allah.
Believing women divorced before being touched have no waiting period to count, and are to be given provision and a gracious release.
Allah sets out the women lawful for the Prophet, lets him choose among his wives, then forbids him more wives or exchanges, except those his right hand possesses.
Enter the Prophet's houses only when invited for meals, leave after eating, ask his wives from behind a partition, and never harm him or marry his wives after him.
There is no blame on women before their fathers, sons, brothers, brothers' and sisters' sons, their women and those their right hands possess, and they are to fear Allah.
Allah blesses the Prophet and His angels ask for it, and believers are told to ask Allah to bless him and grant him peace.
Those who abuse Allah and His Messenger are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and those who undeservedly harm believing men and women bear slander and clear sin.
The Prophet is to tell his wives, daughters and believing women to draw their outer garments over themselves, so they will be known and not abused.
If hypocrites, the sick-hearted and rumor-spreaders in al-Madinah do not stop, they will not stay neighbors for long, and wherever found will be accursed, seized and massacred.
